sections.title: Definition & Epidemiology
sections.content: Choroidal melanoma arises from uveal melanocytes. It is the most common primary intraocular malignancy in adults (incidence ~6 per million). Risk factors include fair skin, light iris color, BAP1 mutation (hereditary), and ocular/oculodermal melanocytosis. Peak incidence is in the 6th decade of life.

sections.title: Red Flags: High Risk Features
content: Symptoms: Photopsia, visual field defects, or blurry vision
Margins within 3mm of the optic disc or fovea

content.explanation: To Find Small Ocular Melanoma: Thickness > 2mm, Fluid (subretinal), Symptoms, Orange pigment, Margin < 3mm to disc, Ultrasonographic hollowness, Halo absence, Drusen absence.

sections.title: Recent Landmark Studies
content: COMS (Collaborative Ocular Melanoma Study): No mortality difference between I-125 plaque and enucleation for medium tumors.
LAG-3 inhibitors (Relatlimab/Nivolumab): Emerging standard for metastatic disease.
Gene Expression Profiling (GEP): Class 1 (Low risk) vs Class 2 (High risk for mets).
